刈 concerns cutting growing things: mowing grass, clipping hair, or reaping crops. The native verb 刈る かる retains a cutting action; it is not a general word for every method of harvesting.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: Picture the two crossed strokes on the left as growth to be clipped beside the upright knife form 刂 on the right. The indexing radical is 刀; 刂 is its right-hand form. This shape association is a memory aid, not a reconstruction of the character's history.
ガイ
刈除 がいじょ — removal; cutting off; mowing
カイ
刈除 かいじょ — an alternative reading of the same word
か.る
刈る かる — mow; clip; reap

Focus practice on かる. The two on readings are retained for recognition: JMdict records both がいじょ and かいじょ for 刈除, without a spelling or sense restriction separating them. This does not establish how often either is used. In 刈る, 刈 supplies か and る is the written verb ending.
刈る かる — mow; clip; reap
稲刈り いねかり — rice reaping; rice harvesting
The object helps with the English translation: 草を刈る (くさをかる) is mowing grass, 髪を刈る (かみをかる) is clipping hair, and 稲を刈る (いねをかる) is reaping rice plants. See the linked verb article for complete examples.
切, "cut," has a broader range. Compare 刈's crossed left strokes and separate upright 刂 with 切's left part and bent 刀 on the right.
乃, "thereupon; possessive no," 凹, "concave; sunken," and 凸, "convex; protruding," do not mean mowing or reaping.
Learn 刈る as a godan verb: 刈ります (かります), 刈った (かった), 刈らない (からない). These inflections do not add new dictionary readings.

Metadata: KANJIDIC2, 2026-11-02 snapshot. Word families: JMdict, entries 1209540, 1209550 and 1167840. Native verb usage: Digital Daijisen and Nikkoku, 刈る. The ガイ compound is also recorded by Jitsu, 刈除; that heading does not independently verify カイ.
刈る かる — mow; clip; reap

刈る means to cut grass, hair, crops, or similar growth: to mow, clip, shear, or reap according to the object. It is a transitive godan verb. The thing cut takes を; the polite form is 刈ります (かります), the past 刈った, and the negative 刈らない.
庭の草を刈りました。 (にわのくさをかりました。) - I cut the grass in the garden.
夏なので、髪を短く刈りました。 (なつなので、かみをみじかくかりました。) - Since it is summer, I had my hair cropped short.
短く describes the resulting short length in the second example.
刈 represents cutting or reaping. It supplies the native stem か, followed by the kana ending る. There is no multi-kanji compound to decompose.

切る (きる) is the broader verb for cutting. It works with many objects that do not suit 刈る, such as a sheet of paper. 髪を切る, "cut one's hair," does not specifically present the haircut as cropping or clipping.

The object helps determine the English verb: 草を刈る is mowing or cutting grass, while 稲を刈る (いねをかる) is reaping rice plants. Do not extend the English gloss "harvest" to every crop or method of gathering food. 刈る retains a cutting action, rather than simply collecting something that has grown.
